chunks: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Shihab ibn 'Abd Rabbih, who said:
Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said: “O Shihab, I like that when I have performed the maghrib prayer, I see a star in the sky.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The basis of recommendation in this report is that a person should proceed calmly in his prayer and perform it with deliberation, for if he does that, his finishing it will be at the time of the appearance of the stars.

key_terms.تُؤَدَةٍ: deliberation, calmness, and unhurried composure in performing the prayer
key_terms.كَوْكَبًا: a star visible in the sky

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith about seeing a star after maghrib prayer mean?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates a recommended practice related to the maghrib prayer, namely performing it with calmness and deliberation. Shaykh al-Tusi explains that the meaning is not delaying the prayer improperly, but praying it in a measured manner such that one finishes around the time the stars become visible.
